Point of Application & Direction: Applied simultaneously vertically and horizontally, or in any direction at the top of the handrail or guard to produce maximum load effect
Concurrency & Exceptions: Not required to act concurrently with the 200 lb concentrated load. See Exceptions 1 and 2.

Element / Load Case: Handrails and Guards - Uniform Load (Exception 1: Residential/Private)
Point of Application & Direction: N/A - Governed by 200 lb concentrated load only
Concurrency & Exceptions: Applies to one- and two-family dwellings (IRC / Group R-3) and within individual dwelling units in Group R-2, and Group I-3, F, H, and S occupancies not accessible to the public.

Element / Load Case: Handrails and Guards - Uniform Load (Exception 2: Assembly Fixed Seating)
Point of Application & Direction: Guards at the front of bleachers, grandstands, and folding/telescopic seating
Concurrency & Exceptions: Shall be designed for 50 plf vertical AND 50 plf horizontal acting simultaneously.

Point of Application & Direction: Applied in any direction at any point along the top of the handrail or guard to produce maximum load effect on the element being considered (post top, rail midspan, wall bracket)
Concurrency & Exceptions: Required for ALL occupancies including one- and two-family dwellings. Not concurrent with the 50 plf uniform load.

Element / Load Case: Guard Infill Components (Balusters, Panel Fillers, Intermediate Rails)
Point of Application & Direction: Applied horizontally normal to the infill component over an area not to exceed 12 in. x 12 in. (1 sq ft) at the most critical location
Concurrency & Exceptions: Need not be assumed to act concurrently with Uniform (1607.9.1) or Top-Rail Concentrated (1607.9.1.1) loads.

Load Type: Safety Factor on Concentrated & Uniform Loads
Point of Application & Direction: Glass used as a structural baluster or panel supporting the top rail (unless a top rail remains in place if any single glass panel fails)
Concurrency & Exceptions: Each glass panel and support frame shall be designed using a factor of safety of 4.

Point of Application & Direction: Measured vertically from adjacent walking surface or line connecting leading edges of stair nosings
Concurrency & Exceptions: Standard minimum guard height for commercial and public areas.

Element / Load Case: Minimum Guard Height - Residential Within Dwelling Units (Group R-2 / R-3)
Point of Application & Direction: Measured vertically from deck/floor surface (34 in. to 38 in. for stair guards/handrails)
Concurrency & Exceptions: Permitted within individual dwelling units in Group R-2 and R-3 (Note: 2025 California Residential Code / CBC may require 42 in. for exterior decks in specific jurisdictions; verify local amendment).

Point of Application & Direction: Openings shall not allow passage of a 4-inch diameter sphere from walking surface to required guard height
Concurrency & Exceptions: 4-3/8 in. sphere permitted at stair open risers; 6 in. sphere at triangular opening formed by riser, tread, and bottom rail.

Element / Load Case: Footnotes & Design Notes (2024 IBC Section 1607.9 / 2025 CBC / ASCE 7-22 Section 4.5.1):
[1] Live Load Factor (LRFD vs. ASD): Handrail and guard loads in IBC Section 1607.9 are live loads (L). Under LRFD, apply load factor 1.6L; under ASD, apply load factor 1.0L.

[2] Wood Load Duration Factor (NDS Table 2.3.2): Because the 200 lb concentrated load or 50 plf guard load represents a short-term human impact/occupancy event, CD = 1.00 (occupancy live load) is standard; some jurisdictions permit CD = 1.60 only if explicitly treated as impact/wind, so default to CD = 1.00 for conservative wood connection design.

[3] Exterior Guard Wind Check: For solid, glass, or high-solidity exterior guards/windscreens on decks and balconies, C&C wind pressure (ASCE 7-22 Chapter 30 or Figure 29.3-1/29.4-2) over tributary post spacing S * H_guard must be checked against the 50 plf / 200 lb live load case.
